title: Parkinson disease: adjunctive metformin pilot

Q01.answer: Test adjunctive metformin in Parkinson disease receiving levodopa/carbidopa. The report identifies UPDRS improvement as primary and circulating biomarkers as secondary; registration NCT05781711 is given. Clinical symptom improvement, with biological hypotheses evaluated separately. A biomarker finding cannot replace the primary clinical comparison.

Q02.answer: Human adults at least 50 years old with diagnosed Parkinson disease. Single Tanta University outpatient center in Egypt; diabetes, atypical/secondary parkinsonism and several comorbidities excluded. 60 randomized, 30 per arm; 27 metformin and 25 control analyzed after withdrawals. The pilot population is narrower than all people with Parkinson disease.

Q03.answer: Glucophage metformin tablets, Mina Pharm, Egypt. Oral 500 mg twice daily for 3 months. Both arms received levodopa/carbidopa 250/25 mg three times daily; unnecessary medicines stopped beforehand. Clinical and blood measurements at baseline and month 3. This tests addition to symptomatic treatment, not replacement of that treatment.

Q04.answer: Levodopa/carbidopa plus placebo. Parallel allocation, 30 participants per arm. Computer-generated random sequence with permuted blocks; an unblinded pharmacist supplied treatment. Participants and medical professionals blinded; pharmacist not involved in outcome assessment. Recruitment June 2023-August 2024, with 3-month individual follow-up. The report does not fully describe block sizes or every concealment safeguard.

Q05.answer: UPDRS improvement primary; TLR4, BDNF, HMGB1 and alpha-synuclein secondary. UPDRS total/subscales, Hoehn-Yahr and Schwab-England; serum ELISA assays. Baseline and 3 months. Clinical symptom/function measures versus circulating surrogate biomarkers. No prespecified minimal clinically important between-group difference is supplied. Disease modification was not directly established by the design.

Q06.answer: UPDRS median (IQR): metformin 152 (129-166) to 128 (98-151); control 141 (115-164) to 139 (101-151.5). Outcome denominators were 27 metformin and 25 control. Post-treatment rank-biserial correlation r=0.106; between-arm P=0.515 for total UPDRS. Within-metformin P=0.001 does not demonstrate superiority. All listed clinical post-treatment between-arm comparisons were nonsignificant. Confidence intervals for the between-arm clinical effect are not supplied. Table 3 labels all four serum markers ng/mL; reported post-treatment between-arm P values are 0.03 for alpha-synuclein, 0.02 BDNF, 0.03 HMGB1 and 0.04 TLR4. They do not prove clinical benefit.

Q07.answer: Five control participants needed additional amantadine; two metformin participants changed to combined treatment and one did not attend. Withdrawals were excluded rather than imputed. Pill counts and calls every 2 weeks monitored adherence; seven consecutive days off treatment triggered withdrawal. Clinical deterioration and treatment changes led to outcome-related exclusions. Per-protocol analysis of 52 completers. Individual participants; repeated blood markers and scores are not independent participants. Outcome-related attrition weakens the randomized comparison and may bias either direction.

Q08.answer: Participants queried for adverse effects at visits and calls every 2 weeks. Table 4 reports 27 metformin and 25 control completers, not all 60 randomized participants. Metformin/control counts: nausea 6/5, diarrhea 4/2, vomiting 5/3, hypotension 9/5, delusions 5/3, abdominal pain 8/5. The described withdrawals mainly involved clinical progression or treatment changes; systematic graded safety data for all randomized participants are not provided. Three months. Nonsignificant safety comparisons in this small completer sample do not establish equivalent safety.
locators: Section 2.6; Table 4, PDF p8, visually checked

Q09.answer: Small single-center pilot, completer exclusions and limited concealment detail. Randomization reduces initial confounding, but post-randomization exclusions and uncontrolled diet/metabolic factors remain. The current NCT05781711 record agrees on 3-month UPDRS and secondary biomarkers; historical versions were not available in this packet. Numerous clinical subscale and biomarker tests without a described multiplicity correction. Small sample and no clinical effect CI limit exclusion of clinically relevant effects. BDNF within-arm P is 0.003 in Table 3 but 0.0003 in prose; baseline ALT/AST P values also differ between prose and Table 1. Preserve table-specific numbers and these discrepancies; do not choose the more favorable P value.

Q10.answer: Older adults without diabetes on levodopa/carbidopa at one Egyptian center. One oral dose and one 3-month duration, not all metformin regimens or formulations. Symptom scores and blood biomarkers do not establish slower long-term progression. No demonstrated clinical superiority; external applicability and durability uncertain. A mechanistic rationale remains hypothesis-generating.

Q11.answer: NCT05781711 / CP016-ARTICLE. The 2016 mouse study is a separate preclinical source, not a companion human trial. One pilot supplies these multiple outcomes; no independent clinical replication is created by multiple citations. Current guide references and the retrieved PubMed/Europe PMC record were checked; no exhaustive clinical search claimed. Keep preclinical support and this small clinical experiment distinct.

Q12.answer: Hayam Ali AlRasheed and colleagues, including Mostafa Bahaa and Mahmoud Abdallah. Tanta University clinical setting, with collaborating institutions. Acknowledges Princess Nourah research support PNURSP2025R485 and AlMaarefa University support. Study identifies Glucophage and Sinemet products; a donation is not established from these brand names. Authors declare no commercial or financial relationships that could constitute a conflict. The disclosure is an author statement, not an independent absence-of-conflict audit.

Q13.answer: Published 2025 Frontiers in Pharmacology report DOI 10.3389/fphar.2025.1497261. Full PDF and XML inspected; numerical Tables 1-4 were visually checked on PDF pp6-8. No required separate supplement was identified in the inspected article. NCT05781711 current record inspected: first posted March 23, 2023, before June 6, 2023 start; UPDRS primary and biomarkers secondary at 3 months. Registry last updated October 30, 2026. No separate protocol file listed; this is not a historical-version audit. No correction/retraction surfaced in the retrieved metadata or article; this is a bounded check, not a guarantee. Source retrieval November 3 and assessment November 4, 2026. The study has a source-specific appraisal; independent verification remains pending.
locators: Full PDF/XML; registration statement; source receipts

Q14.answer: Parkinson clinical benefit and biomarker hypotheses. Supports reported biomarker differences; does not demonstrate superior clinical UPDRS outcomes or disease modification. The authors acknowledge no significant between-group UPDRS difference; the editorial conclusion agrees and rejects within-arm efficacy inference. Replace vague pending placeholders with this distinction.

Q15.answer: This pilot does not establish metformin as an effective Parkinson treatment. Longer-term clinical benefit, tolerability in broader populations and biomarker meaning remain uncertain. Larger blinded trials with intention-to-treat estimates, complete harms and clinically important effect thresholds could change this view. No personal dosing recommendation follows from the pilot.

appraisal: Clinical superiority was not demonstrated. Outcome-related completer exclusions, short duration, multiple biomarker tests and missing confidence intervals limit interpretation. Biomarker units and table-specific findings are now verified; narrative/table P-value discrepancies remain documented.
